blocks.explanation:
A cosine of \(2x - 1\) equals a linear expression, so we solve it graphically.
We need every \(x\) in \([0, \pi]\) where \(y = \cos(2x - 1)\) meets the line \(y = \frac{x}{5}\).
Plan: shapes, table of values, graph, refine to 2 d.p., check.
steps:
Given: \(\cos(2x - 1) = \frac{x}{5}\), \(x \in [0, \pi]\).
To find: all \(x\) in the interval that satisfy it.
Method: Plot \(y = \cos(2x - 1)\) and \(y = \frac{x}{5}\) on the same axes and read the x-coordinates of the intersection points. Use \(d = \cos(2x - 1) - \frac{x}{5}\) to locate the crossings.

Shape of each graph
\(y = \cos(2x - 1)\): amplitude 1, period \(\frac{2\pi}{2} = \pi\). It is highest (1) where \(2x - 1 = 0\), i.e. \(x = 0.5\), and lowest (\(-1\)) where \(2x - 1 = \pi\), i.e. \(x = \frac{\pi + 1}{2} \approx 2.07\). At both ends it equals \(\cos 1 \approx 0.54\).
\(y = \frac{x}{5}\): a line through the origin with slope \(\frac{1}{5}\); it rises from 0 to \(\frac{\pi}{5} \approx 0.63\).
Why: The period \(\pi\) means exactly one full wave fits in \([0, \pi]\).

Table of values (radians, 2 d.p.)
\(x = 0\): \(\cos(2x - 1) = 0.54\), \(\frac{x}{5} = 0\), \(d = 0.54\)
\(x = 1\): \(0.54\), \(0.20\), \(d = 0.34\)
\(x = 1.5\): \(-0.42\), \(0.30\), \(d = -0.72\)
\(x = 2\): \(-0.99\), \(0.40\), \(d = -1.39\)
\(x = 3\): \(0.28\), \(0.60\), \(d = -0.32\)
\(x = \pi\): \(0.54\), \(0.63\), \(d = -0.09\)
Why: \(d\) changes sign only between 1 and 1.5. Near \(x = \pi\) the wave climbs again but only reaches 0.54, while the line is already at 0.63, so there is no second crossing inside the interval.

Draw both graphs and read the intersection
From the figure the wave cuts the line once, on its way down:
\[x \approx 1.17\]
Why: There is only one intersection point in \([0, \pi]\), so there is only one root.

Refine to 2 decimal places
\(d(1.165) = +0.006\), \(d(1.175) = -0.016\)
Why: The sign changes between 1.165 and 1.175, so the root (\(1.1676\ldots\)) rounds to 1.17.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = cos(2x minus 1) (blue wave: 0.54 at x = 0, peak 1 at x = 0.5, lowest minus 1 near x = 2.07, back to 0.54 at x = pi) and the line y = x/5 (pink, from 0 at the origin to about 0.63 at x = pi). They meet once, at x about 1.17, marked with a dashed line to the x-axis.
answer_figure.caption: Exercise 10.2 Q2: y = cos(2x − 1) and y = x/5 on [0, π]; one intersection (original drawing)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints \(x = 1.16\) radians. The root is \(x = 1.1676\ldots\) (\(d(1.165) = +0.006\), \(d(1.175) = -0.016\)), which rounds to \(1.17\). At \(x = 1.16\) the two sides are \(0.248\) and \(0.232\), not equal. Correct answer: \(x \approx 1.17\) radians.
